evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:1 — the whole feature is one self-contained route directory
app/src/routes/layout.tsx:12-24 — nav contains only Pokémon and Types, no abilities link to unwind
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:225-234 — the only cross-feature link to /abilities lives in the Pokémon page's Abilities section
app/src/components/cards.tsx:19 — 'Hidden ability' note rendered by the shared card component, exists only for the abilities feature
app/src/lib/types.ts:26 — Card.hidden flag and lib/server-api.ts:111-124 cardsFor hidden param would be dead after removal
app/src/global.css:204 — .card-note styles in the single stylesheet would be orphaned
removability.rationale: Deleting a route directory plus one section on the Pokémon page removes the feature, but the shared Card abstraction and the flat stylesheet both carry ability-specific residue (hidden flag, .card-note CSS) that becomes dead code unless you also clean it.

evidence: app/src/lib/server-api.ts:67 — spriteUrl() is the single sprite derivation; every card list goes through it
app/src/lib/server-api.ts:120 and :163 — but the Card object literal is constructed in two places, so a card-shape fix lands twice
app/src/lib/server-api.ts:15-37 — apiBase(), CACHE_TTL_MS and the api() funnel: an API base/caching change is one file
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:90-141 — heavy `any` in loader bodies means the compiler won't flag data-shape changes
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:35-38 and app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:20-23 — identical effect-fallback expression duplicated across two pages
changeability.rationale: Most fixes (sprites, base URL, caching, humanization) land in one obvious place thanks to the server-api funnel and shared components, but card construction is duplicated and the `any`-typed loaders quietly remove the type checker from the loop.

evidence: app/src/lib/types.ts:1-40 — components receive narrow typed props (Card, TypeRef, MoveRow, MoveTableData) rather than raw API JSON
app/src/components/cards.tsx:1-5 — client components import only format helpers and types, never server-api
app/src/lib/server-api.ts:1-37 — server access, env var and cache are module-private behind api()/cardsFor() and used only inside routeLoader$ bodies
app/src/routes/layout.tsx:4-6 — browser cache policy declared separately from the server data cache
app/src/components/section.tsx:1-7 — Section is a pure Slot wrapper with a two-prop contract
coupling.rationale: Textbook separation: server data access, client components and shared formatting are distinct layers with explicit interfaces, shared state is only the routeLoader payload, and no component reaches into another module's internals.

evidence: app/src/components/cards.tsx:15-33 — PokemonCard/CardList stretch across home, moves, abilities and types without flag proliferation
app/src/lib/server-api.ts:111-127 — cardsFor takes a narrow {url, hidden?} ref interface, reusable for any 'list of Pokémon refs' source
app/src/components/type-badge.tsx:6-19 — the optional link flag matches real variation (card pills vs linked badges)
app/src/lib/types.ts:26 and app/src/components/cards.tsx:19 — Card.hidden exists solely for the ability page's note, a feature-specific flag leaked into the shared type
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:35-38 vs app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:20-23 — effect-fallback logic copy-pasted rather than factored into server-api
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions are designed around the app's real variation and stretch well (an Items section would reuse Section, CardList, cardsFor and the localization helpers), but the small copy-paste of the effect fallback and the ability-only hidden flag on Card show the seams starting to creep.

findings.issue: The Card literal (id/name/label/sprite) is constructed in two places, so any change to how cards are built or how sprites are chosen must be applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a makeCard(id, name, extra?) helper in server-api.ts and have cardsFor and speciesIndex both use it.

findings.issue: Loader bodies map raw API JSON with `any` throughout (also in abilities/[name]/index.tsx:16, types/[name]/index.tsx:27), so the compiler cannot catch API-shape regressions when editing.
findings.suggestion: Add minimal interfaces for the API records (Species, Pokemon, Ability, Type) to lib/types.ts and type the api() call sites.

findings.issue: The short_effect || flavor text || em-dash fallback is duplicated verbatim in the abilities page (abilities/[name]/index.tsx:20-23); a change to fallback rules fixes only one page.
findings.suggestion: Move a shortEffect(record) helper into lib/server-api.ts next to english() and latestFlavorText().

findings.issue: Card.hidden and the 'Hidden ability' note (components/cards.tsx:19, server-api.ts:111-124) are ability-page-specific knowledge living in the shared card abstraction; removing Abilities leaves dead fields and dead CSS (global.css:204).
findings.suggestion: Either render the note from a per-page slot/prop, or accept the flag but remove it together with the feature (and the .card-note rules).

findings.issue: All styles for every component live in one flat, unscoped stylesheet, so feature removal and renaming leave orphaned rules that nothing flags.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate component styles (useStyles$/scoped CSS or per-component files imported by the component) so styles are deleted with their owners.

findings.issue: The home loader calls allTypes() and allGenerations() that speciesIndex() also fetches internally; the data flow is duplicated knowledge (currently harmless because of the API cache).
findings.suggestion: Have speciesIndex return or have a single loader derive type/generation options from one shared fetch, or add options params to it.

findings.issue: Query parameter names are known in two spots in the same file (homeHref sets them, the loader reads them), a small rename hazard.
findings.suggestion: Define the param names as constants used by both homeHref and useHome.

summary: A well-layered Qwik City app where server data access, presentation components and formatting helpers are cleanly separated, and the highest-value seams (sprite derivation, API base/caching, card lists) are single points of change. Editability is held back by duplicated Card construction in two builders, pervasive any-typing in loaders, and a couple of small copy-pastes and an ability-specific flag on the shared Card type. All five scenarios land in one or two obvious files.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Deleting the route directory plus the Abilities section on the Pokémon page (lines 225-234) removes the feature and all links; the nav never linked it. The remaining work is cleanup of the now-dead hidden flag (cards.tsx:19, types.ts:26, server-api.ts:113-119) and .card-note CSS — easy but easy to miss.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: spriteUrl() (server-api.ts:67) is the only place a card sprite is derived, and both card builders (cardsFor:120, speciesIndex:163) sit in the same file, so one fix covers the home, moves, abilities and types lists — they all render through the same CardList component.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: One line in cardsFor's sort (server-api.ts:125) covers the moves/abilities/types lists; the home page needs its own sort in useHome before the pagination slice (routes/index.tsx:49-56) because CardList can't reorder across server-side pages. Two spots, both discoverable.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: Section, CardList, NotFound, TypeBadge, orDash, pageTitle and the api/slug/english/englishName/latestFlavorText helpers all reuse as-is, and the type list page is a ready-made skeleton for /items. The detail page adapts (not shares) the moves page's ~100-line loader+template — there's no generic resource-detail abstraction, and the effect-fallback expression would likely get a third copy unless it's factored out first.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: apiBase() (line 15), CACHE_TTL_MS (line 7) and the cache Map (line 18) are the only places that know; every request funnels through api() (line 27). The layout's cacheControl is a separate browser-cache concern, correctly not entangled.
